full_frozen_target: One finite universal integer Lambda works in every infinite-dimensional real Banach B: a Lipschitz image of [0,1], doubling in the ambient norm at every scale, with no finite-distortion bilipschitz embedding into any finite-dimensional real normed space.
ball_convention: Closed balls in the actual metric; centers are in the metric type. For subtype spaces these are actual points of the subset. A recentered cover additionally returns membership of every center in the covered set.

groups.candidate_interface: Lemma 1 packing and all repeated covers
groups.contract: Covers uses actual finite center sets and closed distance inequalities. Refinement gives N*M centers; q halvings give D^q centers at radius r/2^q.

Recentering constructs representatives inside the covered set, bounds their cardinality, and pays radius 2Kr. Arbitrary metric subsets inherit D^2 doubling. Surjective placements with dist<=dist(image)<=2dist yield D^4 doubling.
A finite strictly s-separated set covered by balls of radius t with 2t<=s has cardinality at most the number of centers. Iterated doubling gives D^q packing when 2R/2^q<=s.

groups.candidate_interface: Lemma 1 intermediate/high scales; Section 3 cluster scales
groups.contract: For dyadic(k)=1/2^k, any finite index set in (L,U] has at most q members when U<=2^q L. Specializations prove 8 intermediate scales, 4 high-center scales, and 5 cluster scales. Finiteness of the input index set is an explicit hypothesis.

Any real normed-space segment of length at most 2r has a finite cover by at most five closed r/2 balls with centers on that segment, including degenerate segments. Identifying an arbitrary ball intersection with such a segment is external.

groups.candidate_interface: Lemma 1 parent projection and height constraints
groups.contract: For a lineMap parameter in [0,1] and parent length<=2s, horizontal displacement is<=2s. The scalar height (1+theta)s within r of h forces (h-r)/2<=s<=h+r. The Hilbert-product distance-to-coordinate implication is external.

Actual metric triangle bounds control grouped endpoints. Scalar squared-distance hypotheses imply strict r/2 bottom-group and r/16 fine-edge bounds. Their Hilbert orthogonal-product formulas are not proved here.
Actual metric root/point distance inequalities give 97a/200 separation; two points in the same radius-r ball force a<=400r/97. Identifying roots with a fixed unit-vector ray is external.

For natural D>=1, low/high totals are bounded by 81D^10/48D^10 and hence256D^10. Definitions preserve lambda=76800, D=lambda^2, Delta=256D^10 and Lambda=10+6Delta^8. graph_count assumes the relevant finite cover count; it does not construct G or prove its doubling.
